AlternateTargets: has nothing to do with it
Senses.Explanation: There is none (沒) of the dealings, involvement, connection, or bearing named by the compound (交涉): 'there is no connection' or 'it has no bearing.' The records deploy this one literal sense in two ways. First, as a plain statement of no connection. Shitou says that speech and action have no connection (言語動用沒交涉), and his disciple replies that non-speech and non-action also have no connection (非言語動用亦沒交涉). Another line says, 'before the King of Awe-Voice, no connection' (威音已前沒交涉). Second, as a dismissive verdict on a wrong answer. Blue Cliff Record comments repeatedly use 'well, no connection!' (且喜沒交涉 / 且得沒交涉), meaning that the offered account misses the recorded matter. The verdict can itself be challenged: when a monk says 'well, no connection' (且得沒交涉), Yuanwu asks, 'Where is there no connection?' (什麼處沒交涉). Intensified forms include 'utterly no connection' (全沒交涉 / 總沒交涉, 82 combined instances in the cited count), often in the line that something has utterly no bearing on one's own share (於自己分上全沒交涉). The rhetorical question 'what connection is there?' (有甚麼交涉 / 有什麼交涉, 114 occurrences of each graph form in the recorded count) states the same absence by question. The headword occurs 1,389 times in 244 allowlist texts.
Senses.Note: One meaning, 'no connection' or 'no bearing,' with two deployments: a flat statement and a dismissive verdict. Counted forms include 'well, no connection' (且得沒交涉), 37; 'utterly no connection' (全沒交涉), 21; 'altogether no connection' (總沒交涉), 93; 'completely no connection' (了沒交涉), 42; and 'a place of no connection' (沒交涉處), 14. It is corpus-wide rather than an individual signature.

Senses.Explanation: The expression denotes with no handle to grasp in these Chan records. Its wording is there is no nose-handle: no projecting part by which the thing can be seized or led. Frozen-corpus concordance: 197 exact hits in 93 storage files representing 91 independent works. Chan records apply it to sayings, circumstances, people, and what a listener confronts. Dahui pairs it with 'no flavor' and says there is nothing to grasp when considering the dry shit-stick or the raised saying. Another record reverses the phrase into a place of inquiry: 'investigate until there is no handle; precisely where there is no handle is good to investigate.' Wuzhun plays the compound against the positive form, saying there is some handle and entirely no handle. This recurring use for the point at which a word or encounter supplies no graspable lead is the corpus-specific extension of the animal-handle image.

Senses.Note: 6 exact full-case witnesses from 6 independent works support this corpus-bounded sense.

Senses.Explanation: The expression denotes has no flavor in these Chan records. Its wording is ‘has no flavor’ or ‘tasteless.’ The corpus predicates it of sayings, inquiry, food imagery, and an interlocutor’s appraisal. A verse on Nanquan’s ‘ordinary mind is the way’ calls it ‘cold and bland, entirely without flavor,’ yet says that each raising is new. Dahui repeatedly places a person at the point where bringing up the matter feels tasteless, like a lump of hot iron or biting an iron spike, and explicitly says that this is then a good place and must not be abandoned. Later records likewise join ‘nowhere to set a hand,’ ‘without flavor,’ and ‘the road of mind cut off’; one calls the sect’s tea and rice iron-nail rice and wood-chip soup, ‘without flavor’ however long chewed, then calls that tasteless place a good state. The phrase can remain an ordinary adverse verdict: after Dahui Zonggao answers with ‘one melon seed, two shell-halves,’ the recorded questioner says ‘no flavor,’ and Dahui Zonggao hisses. Zen usage bends the sensory predicate by applying it repeatedly to words and sustained inquiry, and by recording masters who name the very tasteless point positively. This entry reports those descriptions without recategorizing them.
